headline: Crude Clears $100, Hormuz Fears Cloud the Open
body_html:
Futures point to a cautious Wednesday open as Brent crude breaches the $100-a-barrel threshold for the first time in this cycle, driven by an escalating Middle East conflict that has brought a fresh wave of tanker strikes in the Gulf and Gulf of Oman. Overnight, Iran and U.S. forces exchanged fire on shipping in what analysts are calling the largest coordinated attack on maritime traffic since hostilities began. Strait of Hormuz transit volumes are running below their 10-day average, and transit costs through the waterway have surged, adding a supply-risk premium to every barrel priced this morning.

Tuesday's session offered a preview of the rotation now unfolding. Breadth was decisively negative — 376 names fell against only 168 gainers across our 545-stock universe — yet semiconductors finished atop the sector table, up 1.38%, and energy added 0.62%, lifted directly by the crude spike. Homebuilders bore the worst of it, down 3.05%, followed by software at -2.13% and consumer names at -1.96%, as rate-sensitive and discretionary pockets absorbed the most selling pressure.

At the open, traders will watch oil-levered names and optical-networking stocks, both of which showed outsized Tuesday strength, while healthcare and software laggards remain under scrutiny. Any further deterioration in Hormuz shipping data or additional vessel incidents could accelerate the flight from growth and deepen the defensive tilt already visible in Tuesday's tape. The geopolitical premium now embedded in crude makes this morning's inventory figures and any diplomatic headlines the day's dominant catalysts.

briefs.headline: Brent Tops $100 on Hormuz Squeeze
briefs.body: Brent crude crossed the $100-a-barrel mark overnight as Middle East hostilities intensified and Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic fell below its 10-day average. An executive at ENOC noted that transit costs through the waterway have escalated sharply since the conflict widened, raising concerns about sustained supply disruption.

briefs.headline: Tanker Strikes Mark Sharpest Escalation Yet
briefs.body: Iran and U.S. forces struck merchant vessels in the Gulf and Gulf of Oman in what observers described as the most intense wave of shipping attacks since the war began. Several vessels were disabled by fire, rattling dry-bulk and tanker operators and pushing war-risk insurance premiums higher across the region.

briefs.headline: Semtech Leads Semiconductor Surge With Near-10% Gain
briefs.body: Semtech surged nearly 10% on Tuesday to pace all gainers in our universe, helping lift the broader semiconductor sector by 1.38% — the only major sector to post a meaningful advance on the session. Coherent, an optical-networking supplier, added 7.1%, underscoring continued investor appetite for infrastructure tied to data-capacity build-outs.

briefs.headline: Solar Names Rebound Sharply Amid Energy Rally
briefs.body: Enphase Energy and SolarEdge climbed 6.76% and 6.52%, respectively, as the broader energy complex caught a bid on the crude spike. Bloom Energy, a fuel-cell developer, was the second-best performer in the entire universe, rising 9.63% and reflecting renewed interest in domestic energy alternatives as geopolitical risk reprices supply.

briefs.headline: Healthcare Devices and Staffing Stocks Hit Hard
briefs.body: Stryker fell 8.81% to lead all decliners in our universe, dragging the healthcare sector down 1.78% on the session. Robert Half dropped 7.91%, reflecting mounting concern that a slower hiring environment is pressuring staffing firms; the industrials sector finished down 0.69% as a result.

briefs.headline: Silicon Valley Unveils Low-Cost Cruise Missile Platform
briefs.body: Defense-technology startup Covenant, backed by Silicon Valley investors, disclosed a mass-producible cruise missile designed to undercut traditional procurement costs significantly. The announcement arrives as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East elevate demand for affordable precision-strike capabilities, drawing fresh attention to non-traditional defense suppliers.
